# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding flow** – no documented sequence from sign-up → first class → integration into community (massive churn risk if this is ad hoc)
- **Churn & cancellation protocol** – no standardised win-back triggers, pause mechanics, or exit interview process
- **Coaching standards & quality assurance** – no Class Quality Audit Checklist or weekly coaching task framework means inconsistent member experience
- **Member retention mechanics** – no check-in cadence, milestone tracking, or 30-day goal-setting process; you're likely losing members quietly
- **Referral programme operation** – incentive rules, tracking, fulfillment all likely manual or unmapped
- **Complaints & incident handling** – no formal escalation, documentation, or resolution SOP (liability + retention risk)
- **Data governance** – GDPR/privacy handling, member data access, retention policies not codified
- **Coach development pathway** – no structured progression, skill assessments, or promotion criteria
- **Health & safety incident reporting** – injuries, near-misses, equipment faults (critical for a physical studio)

---

# **Needs updating**

- **Marketing SOPs (6 built)** – likely focused on campaigns; missing: lead nurture sequences, trial-to-paid conversion process, seasonal/promotional mechanics
- **Coach SOPs (20/23)** – missing the weekly task list and development roadmap; probably no standards for class prep, member communication, or upsell consistency
- **Client SOPs (28/38)** – 10 gaps suggest missing: outcomes tracking, transformation pillar definitions, troubleshooting common member issues, milestone celebration protocols
- **Facilities (8/8 complete)** – check if these cover: equipment maintenance logs, deep-clean schedules, member area safety checks, emergency procedures

- **Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now.** Have each coach list every service they deliver (classes, PT, nutrition advice, form checks, challenges, etc.). You'll find gaps and inconsistencies — this is gold. Don't design from theory; build from reality.

- **Price by outcome + time investment, not guessing.** For each service, calculate: coach hourly cost + overhead + what your market pays. A 1-on-1 PT session at £40/hr might actually need to be £60+ to be sustainable. Talk to 3-5 competitors discreetly to anchor pricing, then decide if you're premium or accessible.

- Create a one-page visual chart they can reference: service name → description → who it's for → upsell pathway. Example: *"Group Class (£8/drop-in) → Personal Training (£45/session) → 6-Week Transformation (£400, includes PT + nutrition)."* Coaches sell better when the journey is obvious.

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Action Plan

## REVENUE — URGENT PRIORITY

• **Churn spike in May (12.8%) destroyed that month's revenue trajectory.** Last 3 months (Jul–Sep) average 6.6% churn vs prior 3 (Feb–Apr) at 5.1%. Root-cause that May dip immediately — likely onboarding or class satisfaction issue post-relocation. Fix it and you recover ~£1,500–£2,000/month. Target: <4% churn.

• **Rev/member volatility is dangerous.** Sep hit £132 (good), but Aug collapsed to £106 despite hitting 153 active members — your highest headcount ever. That's a £26 per-member drop. Either payment issues (failed card collections), class underutilization by new members, or hidden cancellations. Audit TeamUp and GoCardless reconciliation immediately. Opportunity: if Aug had been £132/member at 153 active, that's £20,196, not £16,160 — you left ~£4,000 on the table.

• **Price your membership tiers now.** Sep revenue of £22k on 167 members = £132/member, but you're leaving money on the table if you're not tiered (peak/off-peak, founding/standard, class packs vs unlimited). Run A/B test: introduce a "Peak Plus" tier at +£15/month for priority booking + 1 PT session/month. Conservatively: 30% of 167 = 50 members × £15 = +£750/month baseline.

• **Capitalize on Sep's momentum — it's your strongest month.** 167 active members, 6.2% churn, £22k revenue. Identify what drove this (summer retention campaign? new class type? referral push?). Double down on it in Oct and Nov before winter churn hits.

## EXPENSES — SECONDARY PRIORITY (pending clarity on July relocation costs)

• **Studio relocation sunk ~£X — we need actual P&L detail.** You've given bank flows, not profit/loss. To cut costs properly, I need: staffing payroll, class instructor fees, rent, utilities, insurance, and software (TeamUp, Stripe fees ~2.4%, etc.). Request: full P&L for Sep (your best-performing month). **Rule of thumb for women's fitness gyms: aim for 60% gross margin after direct instructor/staff costs.** If Sep's £22k revenue left you with <£13k gross profit, staffing or occupancy costs are too high.
